lanes.name: fired-timer-execution-and-bootstrap
lanes.notes: executeAstTimerJob: rebuild the context from the saved snapshot, evaluate the stored AstNode body, deliver through the shared delivery path. Plus a concrete async factory that installs the catalog and the scheduler. The accepted Lua scripts, backlog caps, 10-minute grace and the at-most-once claim must remain unchanged in behaviour. Includes a private-Dragonfly test marked #[ignore].
leadIntegrationFindings: Lane E's own gap: the factory builds two AstTimerScheduler values over one namespace, so the delivery scheduler learns a new job only at its next reconcile. Verified precisely: reconcile() arms each pending entry with the job's TRUE dueAt, so a timer whose duration is >= RECONCILE_MS (2000 ms) fires at exactly its dueAt, identical to the source's in-process setTimeout arm. Only a timer SHORTER than RECONCILE_MS can fire up to one cadence late. It is never early, never past expiresAt (10 min grace), and at-most-once is unaffected because the claim consumes before execution.

The catalog's own armed map is never drained (no take_due on the catalog's scheduler). It is a harmless in-memory record, not a correctness issue, but it is a divergence from the source's single activeScheduler.

Lead decision: NOT refactored to a shared scheduler. The fix (one Arc<Mutex<AstTimerScheduler>> shared by the catalog and the delivery driver) touches the delivery path of a 55 KB timer runtime that cannot be compiled under the current authoring-only lease, and the bounded sub-2-second deviation does not justify an unverifiable structural change. Recorded as a named gap with the exact fix instead.

Lock-ordering note for whoever applies that fix: the driver must release the scheduler lock BEFORE executing a claimed job, otherwise a timer body that itself schedules a timer would deadlock on the same mutex.

lanes.name: keyword-ingress-and-by-id-body-handoff
lanes.notes: Ports handleKeywords against the real keyword cache (index match -> body by id -> execute with the by-id body -> deliver). Adds execute_command_with_body to runtime/command.rs so a pre-resolved keyword body reaches the same command logic. Includes #[ignore]d private-Mongo tests for the real variable fallback/tombstone/11000, the execution cooldown lock and the keyword counter write, plus a .cjs actual-source oracle.
leadIntegrationFindings: The by-id body handoff is real: handle_keywords resolves each matched body by id through the native keyword cache and hands it to execute_command_with_body without a second lookup by name.

The source's keyword cooldown floor is preserved: Math.max(configured, getMinimumCommandCooldown(plan_tier)) maps to minimum_command_cooldown(plan.as_deref()) - 1 (pro), 3 (premium), 5 (everything else, including a missing plan).
The keyword's fresh count/enabled read stays AFTER the cooldown gate, and the cached body is never used as mutable counter state.

tasks: Real Redis cooldown-lock contention and expiry test (ignored, private loopback Redis): exact source key format command:execution:cooldown:{channelID}:{executionName} via an extracted pub cooldown_key helper, SET NX PX contention, expiry after the PX window, plan-tier floor applied for keywords and not for normal commands.

Schema-valid differences are bugs and are fixed; wrong-typed deviations are pinned and documented as schema-guarded deviations.

Loopback Twitch test for the AST chat delivery path: ephemeral 127.0.0.1 server, TwitchEndpoints::new pointed at it, asserting method, path, query, Authorization header and the JSON body, plus the Twitch error-response mapping.
lanes.notes: Closes the gaps lane F reported. No execution lease: nothing is compiled or run.
leadIntegrationFindings: Lane F2 authored the Redis cooldown-lock test, the plan-floor assertions and the Twitch loopback test, and reported the native-vs-source comparison as incomplete, handing the missing seam to the lead.

The lead implemented the seam: CommandStore gained a default-implemented handoff(&CommandReference, &JsonValue), called as the first statement of execute_command_body - exactly where the TypeScript calls executeCustomCommand, the seam the source fixture replaces. The parser seam cannot supply it because it runs after the gates and does not expose the authorization; CommandReference does.

The comparison is now native-vs-source: native_observations() serializes the native ingress into the source fixture's document shape and the test compares bodies, executions and delivered field by field against the generated oracle, plus asserts both sides saw the same scenarios.

enabled is now judged by JavaScript truthiness (new js_truthy helper in runtime/command.rs), used by both the ingress gate and the command body's enabled gate. The source writes if (!keyword.enabled), so "yes" is truthy and the source still runs the command; the native previously skipped it. No change for a schema-valid boolean.

A missing cmd is a deliberate pinned divergence: the source calls normalizeKeyword(undefined) and throws out of handleKeywords; the native skips the malformed keyword and continues. The comparison asserts the source throws, the native does not, and both request the same bodies and deliver nothing.

A discriminating match-mode scenario was added on both sides: unknown_mode_anywhere uses an anywhere index and the message 'say hello there' with the body's mode still unknown, so a port that falls back to start now fails.

The Redis test drives SET NX PX directly rather than through NativeCommandStore::acquire; the key format and the plan-tier floor are asserted in-process. Neither the Redis test nor the Twitch loopback test has ever run: no execution lease.
